correctness.rationale: For U=im(A), AB is nilpotent iff its restriction T to U is nilpotent. The linear map B -> (AB)|_U is surjective with fiber size q^(n^2-r^2); Fine--Herstein gives q^(r^2-r) nilpotent T, hence q^(n^2-r) candidate B. Removing B=0 and removing B=A exactly when A is nilpotent proves the degree formula. Distinct powers cannot differ by one, so degree recovers rank and nilpotency. Exhaustive checks on M_2(F_2), M_2(F_3), and M_3(F_2) replay successfully.
